sources.entry: transformers - The model-definition framework for pretrained models in text, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal tasks, for inference and training.

summary.one_liner: Hugging Face Transformers is a model-definition framework that provides pretrained machine learning models for text, vision, audio, video, and multimodal tasks, usable for both inference and training.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a centralized library of model definitions for state-of-the-art architectures across text, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal tasks. Offers a high-level Pipeline API for running inference with a single call, such as text generation, speech recognition, image classification, and visual question answering. Supports chat-style prompting with chat-formatted message lists and a command-line chat via `transformers serve`. Gives access to over 1M pretrained checkpoints on the Hugging Face Hub. Model files are designed to be readable and customizable, and the README states they can be used independently of the library. Per the README, model definitions are compatible with training frameworks (such as Axolotl, Unsloth, DeepSpeed, FSDP, PyTorch-Lightning), inference engines (such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI), and libraries like llama.cpp and mlx.
use_cases: run pretrained models for text generation
fine-tuning or training PyTorch models from the Hub
how_to_run: from transformers import pipeline; pipeline(task="text-generation", model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B")
notable: Acts as a shared model-definition pivot used by many training and inference engines
Pipeline API covers text, audio, vision, and multimodal tasks with a few lines of code
Over 1M pretrained checkpoints on the Hugging Face Hub
caveats: The README says the library is not a generic modular toolbox of neural net building blocks; for generic training loops it recommends Accelerate.
Installing from source gives latest changes but the README warns the latest version may not be stable.
keywords: use open source ai models in python
